item.title: The Zelevinsky involution, co-standard modules for quantum affine algebras and interval symmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathscr{F}_n$ be the subcategory of finite-dimensional representations of the quantum loop algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ whose simple modules are indexed by multisegments consisting of intervals $[a,b]$, where $a,b$ are integers and $0<b-a\le n$. We define the co-standard module associated to a multisegment $\mathbf{s}$ to be the tensor product of the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules, associated to the first node of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$, given by the segments of $\mathbf{s}$. Under a suitable (and necessary) restriction on $n$, we show that its socle is isomorphic to the simple module given by the Zelevinsky dual $\mathbf{s}^\dagger$ of $\mathbf{s}$. We then define an involution $\Phi$ of the Grothendieck ring $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ and prove that it maps the class of a simple module to the class of the simple module given by its Zelevinsky dual. We also show that on suitable subcategories $\Phi$ is induced by an exact autoequivalence reversing tensor products, and we give a $t$-analogue of the multiplicity identity in the quantum Grothendieck ring. Motivated by the determinantal formula for alternating snake modules, we realize $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ explicitly inside a polynomial ring in variables indexed by intervals, and, in the spirit of Macdonald's ninth variation of Schur functions, we show that the fundamental modules correspond to analogues of the elementary symmetric functions and the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules to analogues of the complete homogeneous symmetric functions. This is compatible with $\Phi$ and the classical involution $\omega$, and we prove that alternating snake modules give a family of Schur positive symmetric functions extending the skew Schur functions.
item.dc:creator: Matheus Brito, Vyjayanthi Chari

item.title: Lusztig sheaves, local systems, and the extended Springer resolution
item.description: arXiv:2611.05629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Springer resolution of the nilpotent cone is used to give a geometric construction of the Springer correspondence by applying tools in the derived category of perverse sheaves, particularly the decomposition theorem. In this paper we continue earlier work of the authors on the extended Springer resolution, a map introduced by the first author that factors through the Springer resolution. Our first main result shows that applying the decomposition theorem to this map yields a sum of Lusztig sheaves in all Lie types, each corresponding to a triple of so-called minimal cuspidal datum. We also study the simple perverse sheaves that occur as summands of the resulting sheaf. Our second main result proves that every simple perverse sheaf corresponding to orbits that are Levi-regular must occur, generalizing earlier work in the type A setting to all Lie types.
item.dc:creator: William Graham, Martha Precup, Amber Russell

item.title: Root vector localization and minimal nilpotent finite $W$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.05855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(\mathfrak{g}\) be any finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra, let $h^\vee$ be its dual Coxeter number, and let \(e\) be its highest-root vector which is a minimal nilpotent element. In this paper, using a result of Bavula on invariants of commuting locally nilpotent derivations, we show that \[ U(\mathfrak{g})_f \cong \mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1\otimes U(\mathfrak{g},e), \] where the first factor is a polynomial Weyl algebra of rank $h^\vee-2$, the second factor is a Laurent Weyl algebra of rank one, and $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$ is the finite $W$-algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ and $e$. As an application, we prove that if $M$ is a simple infinite-dimensional $\mathfrak{g}$-module with the minimal GK dimension on which $f-1$ acts locally nilpotently, then $M\cong P\otimes V$ for some simple $\mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1$-module $P$ and some finite-dimensional simple $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$-module $V$. We also give a new proof of the Skryabine quivalence and Petukhov's birational decomposition of the quotient division ring of $U(\mathfrak{g})$.
item.dc:creator: Genqiang Liu

item.title: Stable equivalence of quadratic monomial algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.05889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that gentle algebras are closed under derived equivalence. However, it is easy to verify that they are not closed under stable equivalence. We prove that the classes of quadratic monomial, almost gentle and string almost gentle algebras are closed under stable equivalence. In fact, in each of these cases, stable equivalence is characterized by isomorphism after deleting all nodes and removing semisimple direct summands. The underlying isomorphism theorem gives a positive answer to Mart\'inez-Villa's question on selfinjective-free algebras for these classes. We also prove that the nonprojective simple modules form the unique weakly simple-minded system of a quadratic monomial algebra. Consequently, every stable equivalence of Morita type involving such an algebra lifts to a Morita equivalence when neither algebra has semisimple direct summands. Finally, we describe the effect of node deletion on stable categories of Gorenstein-projective modules and singularity categories, and give combinatorial descriptions of the equivalences for almost gentle algebras using marked configurations.
item.dc:creator: Pengyun Chen, Bohan Xing

item.title: Non-admissible smooth irreducible representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ for totally ramified extensions $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p\geq 5$, and let $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a nontrivial finite totally ramified extension. We construct a non-admissible smooth irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$. The construction uses representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O}_F)$ on which the first principal congruence subgroup acts nontrivially, together with a deformation of a diagram indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$.
item.dc:creator: Dayu Huang

item.title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.06325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$. We prove that for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$ there is an indecomposable $A$-module $M$ with $\dim_k M=\kappa$. Over algebraically closed fields, this settles Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture, that every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. To construct these modules, we extend Bongartz's representation embedding from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules without a simple injective summand to such modules of arbitrary dimension. The extended functor commutes with direct sums and filtered colimits and preserves the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules. Applying it to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of every infinite dimension constructed by G\"obel and Simson yields the required $A$-modules.
item.dc:creator: Haruhisa Enomoto

item.title: Arthur packets for $\mathrm{G}_2$ over $p$-adic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.06742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe Arthur packets for the split reductive group $\mathrm{G}_2$ over a $p$-adic field and compute their stable and endoscopic character distributions. The construction uses the twisted Aubert duality recently studied by Cheng--Kaletha. We identify the corresponding Xu packets on $\mathrm{PGSO}_8$ and their triality-twisted characters. We also extend the result to long-root and short-root Arthur packets corresponding to unitary generic representations of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$.
item.dc:creator: Yugo Takanashi

item.title: Quantum error correcting codes from quiver moduli: Grassmannians, cyclic monodromy, and argyle collision divisors
item.description: arXiv:2611.05526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on aspects of a recent diagrammatic field-theory programme for quantum error correction put forward by the first-named author (arXiv:2607.08911), we construct exact finite-dimensional codes from twisted cyclic and argyle quiver moduli on the projective line. A regular fibre of the node-labelled cyclic Hitchin map records the ways to distribute simple spectral zeroes among the arrows with prescribed degrees. The Hilbert space spanned by these allocations is a Young permutation module. Root monodromy acts on its Specht factors and leaves their multiplicity spaces noiseless. Resetting the Specht factor therefore recovers the encoded state for every channel in the monodromy noise model. We prove that the largest Kostka multiplicity is the optimal dimension of a subspace code correcting the full monodromy algebra, even among codes spanning several isotypic blocks. Quantizing an argyle master space recovers the cyclic sheet space as a weight sector of a tensor power, with the identification preserving monodromy. For the balanced three-cycle with $t$ zeroes per arrow, the multiplicity of a partition $(a,b,c)$ of $3t$ is $1+\min(a-b,b-c)$. The optimal logical dimension is thus $t+1$, attained uniquely by the block indexed by $(2t,t)$. At $t=1$ we give explicit codewords for a qubit on six sheets. The commuting right action generates its full logical algebra, yielding errors outside the monodromy model that leave the measured footprint statistics unchanged yet require different recoveries. We also compute collision-parity ranks, give a higher-rank Grassmannian example, and derive a conditional criterion for recovery across splitting types.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rayan, Evan Sundbo

item.title: On the existence of nonadmissible irreducible smooth representations of $p$-adic $\mathrm{GL}_n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.05552v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p>7$ be a prime, let $n>1$, and let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$ not equal to $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For every extension $E$ of the residue field of $F$, we construct an irreducible smooth $E$-representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ which is not admissible. When $E$ is countable, we also construct such representations without a central character and with nonscalar endomorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Le, Mansimar Singh

item.title: Equivariant elliptic cohomology via loop spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a cohomology theory $H_A(-)$ canonically attached to any 1-dimensional commutative group scheme A over a connective $E_\infty$-ring. The additive group in characteristic zero gives 2-periodic de Rham cohomology, the multiplicative group gives topological periodic cyclic homology, and an elliptic curve gives elliptic cohomology. The construction extends to the G-equivariant setting for an algebraic group G, yielding in the elliptic case a theory of equivariant elliptic cohomology on algebraic varieties with G-action that takes values in sheaves on the stack of G-bundles. Over the complex numbers, and for G connected reductive, this lifts Grojnowski's theory from the moduli space of G-bundles to the stack. The key player is the category of perfect complexes on A with 0-dimensional support, equipped with the convolution product induced by the group law of A. It plays the role of a categorified circle and is used to define a loop space $L_A^G(X)$, whose structure sheaf gives rise to $H_A^G(X)$ after periodization. Sheaves on $L_A^G(X)$ equivariant under loop rotation provide a category of coefficients for $H_A^G(-)$ in the same way that D-modules provide coefficients for de Rham cohomology. At the point X = *, the theory also gives rise to an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum (or sheaf thereof) $K_A$, which recovers complex K-theory for $A = \mathbf{G}_m$, and the sheaf $\mathcal{O}^{top}$ of topological modular forms for the universal elliptic curve.
item.dc:creator: Emile Bouaziz, Adeel A. Khan

item.title: Holomorphic flexibility properties of strongly commuting varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.05905v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study holomorphic flexibility properties of the strongly commuting variety of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$. We prove that the smooth locus of the strongly commuting variety of $G$ is Oka-$1$. We also prove that the smooth locus of the commuting variety of a semisimple complex Lie algebra is Oka-$1$, and that it contains a Zariski dense open subset which is algebraically elliptic.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Giannini

item.title: From the quantum group $U_{q^{1/2}}( {\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2 )$ to the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.06256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal A_q$ be the Kronecker quantum cluster algebra with principal coefficients. We construct an explicit algebra homomorphism from the whole quantum group ${U_{{q^{1/2}}}}( {{{\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2}} )$ to $\mathcal A_q$, whose images together with either of the two frozen variables generate $\mathcal A_q$. As an application, we obtain algebra homomorphisms from the split $\imath$quantum groups of affine $\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ to $\mathcal A_q$. Moreover, we explicitly determine the images of the positive and negative real and imaginary root vectors of ${U_{{q^{1/2}}}}( {{{\widehat {\mathfrak{sl}}}_2}} )$ in terms of quantum cluster variables.
item.dc:creator: Junyuan Huang, Xueqing Chen, Ming Ding, Fan Xu

item.title: Identities of Representation of Lie subalgebras of the first Weyl algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.06305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a field. We study weak polynomial identities for pairs $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the first Weyl algebra over $F$ and $V$ is either a Lie subalgebra (under the usual Lie bracket) of $A$, or simply a vector subspace of $A$. Sometimes the weak identities of $(A,V)$, when $V$ is a Lie algebra, are called identities of representations of Lie algebras. Our starting point is the description of finite dimensional Lie algebras $L$ that can be embedded into the first Weyl algebra; this description was given by Rausch de Traubenberg, Slupinski and Tanas\u{a} in 2006. First we assume that $F$ is algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and describe a finite basis of the weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$ where $L=\mathfrak{sl}_2$. In order to obtain such a basis we invoke theorems by Razmyslov and by Trishin concerning the identities of infinite dimensional irreducible representations of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. Afterwards we consider $L$ as a filiform Lie algebra together with its concrete realisation inside the first Weyl algebra. We produce a finite basis of weak identities of the pair $(A,L)$, assuming $F$ to be infinite. Finally we study the weakest form of identities for $(A,V)$ where $A$ is the $n$-th Weyl algebra and $V$ is just a vector space - its canonical generating vector subspace. We deduce a basis of the weak identities in this case as well, once again assuming $F$ to be an infinite field, with no restriction on its characteristic. The same result was recently obtained by Dotsenko and Lopatin in characteristic $0$ by different methods. Our methods are combinatorial, we also use the theory developed by Razmyslov, and the representations of the symmetric and the general linear groups and their duality. We employ the characteristic-free description of the invariants of the symplectic group given by De Concini and Procesi.
item.dc:creator: Vyacheslav Futorny, Plamen Koshlukov, Jo\~ao Fernando Schwarz

item.title: High-Degree Restricted Cohomology for $K(3;1)^{(1)}$ in Characteristics Five and Seven
item.description: arXiv:2611.06396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the high-degree restricted first cohomology of the positive subalgebra of the rank-one contact algebra in characteristics five and seven, with parabolically induced coefficients. In degrees from twice the characteristic through four times the characteristic minus three, each characteristic has six nonzero homogeneous components, of total dimension thirteen. The constituents include Frobenius twists of the natural horizontal module, represented by Cartier cocycles. PBW duality converts the calculation into bounded-degree homology, where the coefficient action couples the natural and cubic relation coordinates. The resulting modules determine the high-degree part of the coefficient cohomology used in the Lyndon-Hochschild-Serre term $E_2^{0,1}$ for extensions of induced contact modules. In particular, extensions from the Steinberg induced modules vanish in these degrees.
item.dc:creator: Chao Ma

item.title: Hessenberg character
item.description: arXiv:2611.06852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group with Borel subgroup $B$, flag variety $\mathcal B=G/B$, and Weyl group $W$. We define the \emph{Hessenberg functor} on the geometric Hecke category by microlocalizing along the diagonal in $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ and pushing forward along the Springer map. It induces the \emph{Hessenberg character} of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra, with values in graded $W$-representations. On Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements indexed by smooth elements of $W$, this character recovers the cohomology of the associated regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties. We identify the Hessenberg functor with the microlocalization of Lusztig's character functor and compute the Hessenberg character using Lusztig's nonabelian Fourier pairing. More generally, for families of Hessenberg schemes defined by pure-dimensional $B$-stable closed cones in the tangent space $T_{eB}\mathcal B$, we show that monodromy on the intersection cohomology of regular semisimple fibers factors through $W$. When the cone is the tangent cone of a Schubert variety, we give a local condition at $eB$ under which the same character formula computes the graded $W$-character of this intersection cohomology. Combined with the methods of Precup and Sommers, our character formula can be used to compute the graded $W$-characters of all regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties in all Lie types of rank at most ten, including all exceptional types. These computations also motivate positivity and unimodality conjectures for Hessenberg varieties and Lusztig varieties in types $B$, $C$, and $D$, together with positivity conjectures for their partial flag versions.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Brosnan, Jaehyun Hong, Donggun Lee

item.title: Noncommutative marked surfaces II: tagged triangulations, clusters, and their symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2507.20393v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of the paper is to define noncommutative cluster structure on several algebras ${\mathcal A}$ related to marked surfaces possibly with orbifold points of various orders, which includes noncommutative clusters, i.e., embeddings of a given group $G$ into the multiplicative monoid ${\mathcal A}^\times$ and an action of a certain braid-like group $Br_{\mathcal A}$ by automorphisms of each cluster group in a compatible way. For punctured surfaces we construct new symmetries, noncommutative tagged clusters and establish a noncommutative Laurent Phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Arkady Berenstein, Min Huang, Vladimir Retakh

item.title: Balanced subsets in root systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.11219v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Balanced and well-balanced subsets of the set of positive roots of compact Lie algebras arise naturally in problems related to Hermitian and spin geometry. In this paper we compute the maximal and minimal size of well-balanced subsets in all simple root systems.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Moroianu, Paul Schwahn

item.title: A subcategory with remarkable homological properties via actions of tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By equipping the category $\mathcal{M}$ of modules over a finite dimensional algebra with the action of a finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$, we introduce a subcategory $\mathcal{PM}$ satisfying numerous remarkable properties: it is generating and cogenerating, functorially finite, closed under Auslander--Reiten translations (i.e. precluster tilting), and it computes the finitistic dimension. Through a functor category perspective, $\mathcal{PM}$ is identified with the $\mathcal{C}$-module functors that are projective, and we also prove a $\mathcal{C}$-equivariant version of the Auslander(--Solberg) correspondence. As examples, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ contains only finitely many indecomposable modules for some tensor product algebras. For some family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer, we show that $\mathcal{PM}$ is exactly the subcategory of $\tau$-locally free modules.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Coulembier, Edmund Heng

item.title: Hybrid Clifford Codes via Operator Algebra Quantum Error Correction and Projective Representation Theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.02531v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Clifford codes are a natural generalization of quantum stabilizer codes based primarily on representation theory. This class of codes has previously been extended to the setting of quantum subsystem codes. We formulate a two-fold generalization of Clifford codes, for both the hybrid classical and quantum information and projective representation theory settings. This leads to new classes of hybrid subspace and subsystem Clifford codes. We extend the fundamental representation theoretic quantum error correction theorem to include these codes, based on the operator algebra quantum error correction framework. We also discuss several examples throughout the presentation, of both stabilizer and non-stabilizer type.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Eidesen, David W. Kribs, Andrew Nemec

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32064v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $\mu=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^\mu, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $\mu$.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano

item.title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41529v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective. In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes. For rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes whose vertices have coordinates that are reciprocals of integers, we show that the resulting numerator is a polynomial and is effective.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Uchiumi
